complexity.notes: Correct but unidiomatic: the standard iterative reversal uses three pointers and O(1) extra space. Appending None into the list and relying on nodes[-1]/nodes[-2] indexing is a clever but convoluted way to get the base cases.
complexity.summary: Collects all nodes into a Python list (with a trailing None sentinel), then rewrites each node's next pointer to the previous node and returns the former tail. Works but uses O(n) extra space.
